title: Simple growth-rate models generate essentially all mollusc shell shapes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Simple growth-rate models generate essentially all mollusc shell shapes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Mollusc shell shapes result from secreting material at different rates around the shell opening, and essentially every form produced by a simple growth model with a few parameters is found in some real mollusc.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The remarkable fact illustrated on the next page is that essentially all of them are found in some kind of mollusc or another.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Growth of Plants and Animals” (from p. 400), p. 415. Scope: coiled shell shapes of molluscs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-22: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The model can be exhaustively sampled and public shell scans permit direct geometric tests. Current collections do not uniformly represent molluscan diversity, and absence from a database is not absence in nature. Mechanism requires developmental observations beyond final-form matching.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Generate the morphology space of the stated few-parameter shell-growth model, embed standardized three-dimensional scans of mollusc shells in the same shape descriptors, and estimate coverage in both directions. Large model regions with no real counterpart or many real shells outside the model would refute essentially complete correspondence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shape agreement does not establish secretion-rate causation.

Museum scans are taxonomically and morphologically biased.

Essentially every form needs a coverage threshold and sampling measure over parameter space.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.52
discriminating power: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.76
data existence: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The model is a small parameter sweep, and public specimen portals contain large numbers of shells across the classical morphospace. That is enough to test occupation of much of the model. It is not enough to certify that essentially every generated form occurs, because rare geometries and photographic gaps remain. The claim is resolvable in large part and not in full.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sample the few-parameter shell-growth model on a grid of expansion, translation, and aperture shape, and ask what fraction of occupied cells have a matching specimen. A match for essentially every cell would support the claim; a substantial region of the model with no real shell would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matching a geometric parameter to a shell is partly a judgment about which coiling features count.

Image coverage is uneven, so an empty cell in the model may be a gap in digitization.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.55
data existence: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.65
